messages:
alex: heads up — ran into a race with the quota finalizer when late tokens arrive after a ledger snapshot.
ben: can you paste the stack/log where it trips?
ale x: here — error happens in finalizer.applyLease(): 
```
WARN finalizer - lease already released for token=tok_3a5f
ERROR attribution - double-claim detected, aborting commit
```
nora: hmm — is that the lazy finalizer path we added to avoid hot checkpoints?
alex: yep. We switch to lazy finalization (defer until watermark) but late-arrivals sometimes trigger a synchronous fallback which races with the lease reaper.
lee: so two flows: 1) late event path that tries to claim credits immediately, and 2) async finalizer that later reconciles and releases lease. If both operate, we can end up double-assigning credits.
chris: is this just an ordering problem (check-then-act) or do we have missing idempotency in the claim flow?
alex: a bit of both. The claim flow relies on lease CAS, but the reaper uses a best-effort tombstone write that doesn't coordinate with immediate claims.
nora: possible mitigations: add a claim-version field on the ledger entry and make finalizer strictly versioned, or push claims through the same coordinator (single writer). Both increase latency/coordination.
ben: what about a short-lived "inflight marker" that blocks reaper for X secs on recent tokens? cheap and localized.
nora: inflight marker reduces races but complicates GC and increases state churn. Also doesn't help if the reaper and claim happen on different regions (cross-region stale clocks).
chris: another idea: allow double-writes but have downstream billing dedupe using attribution proofframes (replay-safe). We already have audit-id + hash envelope in events.
lee: that would push complexity into the audit/reconciliation step. But it's attractive: keep low-latency claims and fix in the recon pipeline.
alex: tradeoffs: 1) stronger coordination = fewer compensations, higher p99 on path; 2) relaxed path + reconciliation = simpler fast path, more complex audits and potential temporary overcharging until recon runs.
ben: product question — is temporary overcharge acceptable if we guarantee eventual correction + clear customer-visible logs?
chris: finance will probably require strong guarantees for enterprise customers. For self-serve, we can tolerate small corrections if we surface them.
lee: implementation proposal: default to relaxed fast-path (deferred reconciliation) with canary 10% of tenants on strict single-writer mode and SLA gating. Then iterate.
alex: for canary we need flags: per-tenant attribution-policy = [fast, strict] and metric hooks. Also a short TTL inflight marker as a safety net.
nora: also add deterministic idempotency key generation in claim RPC: `claimKey = sha256(tenant||eventId||providerEpoch)` so recon can confidently dedupe during audits.
chris: +1 to deterministic keys. That buys cleanup simplicity.
ben: CI bot shows a failing test for cross-region late arrival in the integration suite — @ci-bot can you rerun the relevant e2e with region-fuzz?
ci-bot: running e2e:billing/late-arrival-test with region-fuzz (3 variants) — started 
ci-bot: e2e completed: 2/3 variants passed, 1 failed (timing bucket). Full logs uploaded: https://ci.internal/runs/4620001111
alex: uploaded a repro snippet to the run. Next steps I propose:
- implement deterministic claimKey for claims (low risk)
- add per-tenant policy flag and config for canary
- short inflight marker TTL as defense-in-depth
- route enterprise tenants to strict mode by default

lee: sounds good. Can we get a small RFC PR for the claimKey + policy flags? I can drive the PR for canary infra.
alex: will open RFC today, include perf baseline and reconciliation impact.
nora: add a section about audit downstream: how reconciliation will surface corrections to billing and what SLAs we promise.
chris: note for the RFC: please include the failure telemetry we want (overcharge count, mean correction lag, reconciled delta) so SRE/finance can monitor.
alex: ack. I'll draft and ping everyone. :thumbsup:
audit-bot: note - please tag audits-team if any change touches reconciliation windows or proofframe formats.
ben: tagging audits-team in RFC when ready.
alex: thanks — will follow up with RFC link once opened.
